skill.name: skill-vetter
skill.description: Security-first checklist for vetting OpenClaw skills before installation. It reviews metadata, permissions, red flags, and typosquat risks.
skill.summary: Manual security checklist for reviewing OpenClaw skills before installation.
skill.author: useai-pro

security_audit.summary: The static command, filesystem, sensitive-file, and prompt-injection hits are false positives caused by Markdown examples and defensive checklist text. The skill contains no executable script, network call, or direct secret access request. One semantic issue remains: the community skill self-declares audit trust metadata that could mislead users without independent verification.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the trust-score and last-audited claims, or label them as author-provided metadata until a marketplace verifier confirms them.

static_findings.snippet: - [ ] `name` matches the expected skill name (no typosquatting)
- [ ] `description` is clear and matches what the skill actually does
| `fileWrite` | Medium | Must explain what files are written |
| `network` | High | Must explain which endpoints and why |
| `shell` | Critical | Must explain exact commands used |
Flag any skill that requests `network` + `shell` together — this combination enables data exfiltrati
- Instructions to modify system files (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, crontab)
- Prompt injection patterns ("ignore previous instructions", "you are now...")

semantic_findings.title: Self-attested audit trust metadata
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares audit metadata with a high trust score, last-audited date, and permission claims inside its own frontmatter. In a community skill, self-issued trust claims can mislead users or automated installers unless independently verified.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited frontmatter directly includes audit trust data and permission assertions. The risk is contextual because the repository source is community, so independent verification is required.

content.value_statement: Installing unreviewed skills can expose projects to unsafe permissions, hidden instructions, or typosquat risk. This skill provides a structured checklist for manual pre-install security review.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SKILL.md metadata for name, version, description, and author signals.
Classifies requested permissions by risk and required justification.
Lists critical red flags such as credential paths, obfuscation, unsafe commands, and sandbox bypass requests.
Checks skill names for typosquat patterns and common misspellings.
Produces a manual report with verdict, permissions, red flags, and installation recommendation.
limitations: It is a checklist skill, not an automated malware scanner.
It depends on the reviewer providing the complete skill content.
It cannot verify external author reputation without additional evidence.
It does not execute or sandbox the reviewed skill.

use_cases.title: Review a marketplace submission
use_cases.description: Assess a submitted OpenClaw skill before allowing it into a shared catalog.

use_cases.title: Check a GitHub skill before install
use_cases.description: Review a SKILL.md file from a repository before adding it to a local agent setup.

use_cases.title: Audit installed skills periodically
use_cases.description: Recheck existing skills after version changes or permission updates.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Skill Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one skill file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Vet this SKILL.md before I install it. Focus on metadata, permissions, red flags, and a clear install recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Permission Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill for permission risk. Explain whether each requested permission is necessary and what evidence supports the decision.

prompt_templates.title: Typosquat and Identity Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of source trust and naming.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this skill name, author, and source for typosquat or impersonation risk. Compare it against likely legitimate names.

prompt_templates.title: Full Pre-Install Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full pre-install vetting pass on this skill. Include metadata, permissions, content red flags, typosquat risk, verdict, and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: A developer shares an OpenClaw skill from GitHub and asks whether to install it.
output_examples.output: The review returns a warning verdict, notes unclear authorship, flags broad file access, and recommends sandbox testing before installation.

output_examples.input: A marketplace reviewer checks a SKILL.md that includes shell and network permissions.
output_examples.output: The report marks the permission combination as high risk, asks for exact command and endpoint justification, and recommends blocking until clarified.

output_examples.input: An operator audits an updated skill with a changed name and new instructions.
output_examples.output: The report compares the name for typosquat patterns, reviews the new instructions, and lists any changes that need manual approval.

best_practices: Review the full SKILL.md file, including frontmatter and body text.
Require clear justification for file write, network, shell, and elevated access.
Treat version updates as new reviews when permissions or instructions change.
anti_patterns: Installing a skill based only on popularity or a familiar name.
Ignoring quoted instructions that ask the agent to bypass safety controls.
Approving broad permissions without exact files, commands, endpoints, and reasons.

faq.question: Does this skill scan code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides a manual security review of skill metadata, permissions, content, and naming signals.

faq.question: Can it confirm that an author is trustworthy?
faq.answer: No. It can identify missing or suspicious author information, but external reputation must be verified separately.

faq.question: What permissions does it treat as highest risk?
faq.answer: Shell and network access receive the most scrutiny, especially when both appear together.

faq.question: Does it detect prompt injection?
faq.answer: It tells the reviewer to flag phrases that try to override instructions, change roles, or disable safeguards.

faq.question: Can it review skills for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The checklist is useful for skill files used with Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar agent tools.

faq.question: Should a safe verdict allow automatic installation?
faq.answer: No. A safe verdict supports installation, but users should still follow local approval and sandboxing policies.
